actions.action: Rinse the leaves with lukewarm water
Unpot the plant and check the roots
Trim brown, mushy roots if any are found
Repot into fresh chunky aroid mix with perlite and bark and discard the old soil
Wash the pot or use a new one
Apply a systemic insecticide (acetamiprid or spinosad) or spinosad spray every 5-7 days for 4-6 weeks
Alternatively, release Amblyseius cucumeris predatory mites
Move the plant closer to the window, into bright indirect light and a cooler spot in summer
Check the soil and water only when the top 3-5 cm is dry
Start a dilute fertilizer once steady healthy growth appears
Cut off leaves that are mostly dead
Prune the bare vine back to a node

reason: The answer names thrips as the primary cause and also flags low light; its central advice of repeated thrips treatment plus moving the plant closer to the window matches the fix, and nothing it recommends is likely to harm the plant.
